To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tactile sensitivity enhancement in blind Braille readers is a result of training and that its effects are, in the main, task- and, to a lesser extent, hand-specific.
tactile training in blind and low- vision individuals is associated with enhanced tactile sensitivity in both hands and that the enhancement is task-specific.
tactile experience in blind individuals enhances tactile sensitivity in the trained hand and that this effect is task-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain is able to reorganize itself after damage or loss of sensory input.
the question of whether the tactile sensitivity enhancement (TSe) observed in blind Braille readers is a specific or more general effect of tactile training.
the behavioral manifestations of brain plastic in blind and low vision people, and with the effects of tactile training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tactile experience is a necessary, but not a sufficient condition for the development of TSE.
the effects of training in Braille are specific, but not entirely specific.
tactile training in Braille readers is of significance in tactile sensitivity enhancement (Tse), but its effects are to a large extent task- and hand specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of tactile training are specific to the task and the hand used in training, but the effects are also general, in that they are detectable even when the task and/or the hand used in testing is dissimilar from that used in training.
tactile training in blind Braille readers enhances tactile sensitivity, but that this effect is limited to the trained hand and task.
TSE in the Braille system is the result of a complex interplay of several factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tactile experience can induce a significant enhancement of tactile acuity.
tactile experience can enhance tactile acuity in blind and low vision individuals and that this enhancement can be observed even when using a hand not previously trained in Braille.
the tactile system is highly plastic and that the effects of tactile training are detectable even in individuals with low vision.
